summary: Day 1 of the 5-session window went the way the risk-off call expected, but only slightly. close.json has the SPY benchmark at 561.03 against 562.66 on 11-24, about -0.29%, which puts SPY near 1.9% under the 730.62 200-day, still below the regime line. TLT rose 0.86% on the day while SPY fell, so the flight-to-quality pattern I cited (TLT 5d +2.44% vs SPY 5d -1.86%) held for one more session. The call is graded on cumulative SPY return through about 12-02 (the window spans Thanksgiving: 11-26 closed, 11-27 half day). It is not yet right: SPY needs a further fall of roughly 0.7% or more, and one quiet down day settles nothing.
update: Keep risk-off at about 0.55 for the next run unless the morning packet shows SPY reclaiming 730.62 or VIXY's 5-day return turning negative while SPY's turns positive. The day's single-stock moves are mixed: SAM +2.74% and DPZ +1.46% were up, while INCY -1.02% and IDXX -0.37% were down. They are not sector evidence, so the Staples and Health Care tilts stand on the packet's XLP (+8.98% vs 200-day) and XLV (+15.24%) figures, and the XLV -0.28% 5-day slip is still the thing to watch. Two cautions for tomorrow. (1) The account's SPY series moved -3.6% on 11-20 and then +4.7% on 11-23. With 20-day realized vol at 31.8%, a sharp holiday bounce can turn a 5-day window on its own, so I should not raise confidence on a -0.29% day. (2) Don't count TLT's +0.86% as fresh evidence a second time. It extends the same week the 11-23 to 11-25 notes already cited. The PM's TLT relative clause is still unmet, because TLT beat SPY on the day. My scorecard (12-9, 57.1% vs a 52.4% always-risk-off baseline) beats the baseline by only one call, and all three of my risk-on calls in this drawdown were wrong. So a stance change needs packet evidence of a turn (SPY above its 200-day, falling VIXY, XLK/QQQ 5-day positive), not a feeling that the market is oversold.
